property_summary: For every caller and amount, after calling addToBalance() the reference contract increments the caller's userBalance by the sent value (so getBalance(caller) increases by amount), whereas the mutant that writes to userBalance[address(0)] instead will not increase the caller's balance for some inputs (nonzero amount).

For any caller and any sent amount, after addToBalance() the caller's recorded userBalance equals the sent amount plus their prior balance (i.e., addToBalance increments the caller's balance); the mutant that writes to userBalance[address(0)] breaks this because the caller's balance won't increase for some nonzero amounts.

After any call to addToBalance by any address with any nonzero value, the caller's recorded userBalance equals the ETH sent (i.e., balances only increase by the sent amount and do not change due to re-entrancy); the mutant (which omits setting locked_ = true) allows a re-entrant attacker to manipulate balances and thus can make that equality fail for some inputs.

For any attacker address A and deposit amount v>0, if A calls addToBalance with value v while a separate helper attacker contract (whose receive() re-enters addToBalance) is set as msg.sender for a prior deposit, then after A's deposit the sum of all userBalance entries equals the contract's ether balance; the mutant (missing locked_ = true) allows reentrant manipulation that makes stored balances != address(c).balance for some inputs.

For any attacker address 'atk' and deposit amount >0, if atk calls addToBalance (possibly reentering via a helper that itself reenters on receive) then after the call completes the reference contract's userBalance(atk) is at least the total Ether the attacker ever successfully sent into C (i.e. stored balance never understates cumulative deposits by that address); removing the locked_ = true reentrancy guard allows a reentrant helper to cause stored balances to be smaller than actual ETH received for some inputs.

Invariant: After any single call to addToBalance(msg.value) by an honest depositor (EOA) while no reentrant attacker is executing, the depositor's recorded userBalance equals the cumulative deposits they have made (i.e., userBalance(sender) increases by exactly msg.value); the mutant that fails to set locked_ = true allows a reentrant attacker contract to re-enter addToBalance during another deposit and corrupt stored balances so this equality can fail for some fuzzed deposit amounts and attacker behavior.

For every depositor A and any attacker contract Attacker that may re-enter, after A calls addToBalance with value v (an honest EOA deposit), the stored userBalance for A in the reference equals its previous balance plus v (i.e., a single honest deposit cannot be decreased by concurrent reentrant activity); the mutant that omits setting locked_ = true allows a reentrant attacker to cause userBalance(A) to be less than expected for some inputs.

getBalance(u) returns the actual withdrawable balance of u (i.e., address(c).balance does not exceed the sum of reported balances minus caller refunds), specifically for a funded account: getBalance(u) equals the amount previously deposited by u (no constant offset).
After depositing depositAmount from this test contract into c, getBalance(user) must equal depositAmount.
After depositing depositAmount from this test contract into c, c.getBalance(user) equals depositAmount.
After depositing depositAmount from this test contract into c, getBalance(user) equals depositAmount.
After this contract deposits depositAmount into c, c.getBalance(address(this)) equals depositAmount.

For any address u and any sequence of deposits via addToBalance(), getBalance(u) always returns the exact stored userBalance[u]; the mutant that adds +1 breaks this by returning userBalance[u] + 1 for some inputs (any nonzero balance).

For any queried address u, getBalance(u) returns that address's stored userBalance; the mutant that returns userBalance[msg.sender] breaks this by returning the caller's balance instead of the requested u for some inputs.

For every address u, getBalance(u) returns the stored userBalance[u]; the mutant that always returns 0 breaks this because there exist addresses with nonzero stored balances whose getBalance(u) would wrongly return 0.
For every address u, getBalance(u) returns that address's stored userBalance; the mutant that always returns userBalance[address(0)] breaks this when u != address(0) and userBalance[u] differs.

For every address u, getBalance(u) returns the actual stored userBalance[u]; the mutant that returns double (userBalance[u] * 2) violates this because it yields a different value for any u with non-zero stored balance.

For any caller and any nonzero payable amount, after calling addToBalance the caller's stored userBalance increases by exactly the sent amount (reference holds for all inputs); the mutant that leaves the balance unchanged breaks this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero ETH amount, after calling addToBalance the contract's stored balance for that caller increases by at least the sent amount (reference always holds); the mutant that assigns the slot to itself can leave the stored balance unchanged, violating this rule for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero msg.value, after calling addToBalance() the caller's stored userBalance increases by exactly msg.value (i.e., new balance = old balance + msg.value); the mutant that zeroes the stored balance before adding breaks this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any non-negative deposit amount, calling addToBalance increments that caller's stored balance by exactly the sent msg.value (i.e., final balance == prior balance + msg.value); the mutant that zeroes the stored slot before adding can erase prior balance and thus fails this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, after calling addToBalance the user's stored balance equals the contract's recorded balance for that address (getBalance) and also equals the sum of prior recorded balance and the received msg.value; the mutant that zeroes the slot before adding can cause getBalance to not reflect the actual Ether retained by the contract for that user (address(c).balance vs getBalance mismatch) for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, when the caller sends Ether via addToBalance, the contract's stored userBalance for that caller must equal the cumulative total of all successful addToBalance deposits sent by that caller in the current contract lifetime (i.e., userBalance never decreases as a result of addToBalance); the mutant that sets the stored slot to zero before adding can make userBalance decrease relative to its prior value for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount, immediately after a successful addToBalance call the contract's stored userBalance for that caller equals the previous stored userBalance plus the sent msg.value; the mutant that zeroes the stored slot before adding can cause final stored userBalance to be less than the prior balance + msg.value for some inputs.

For any caller and any ETH amount, after a successful addToBalance call the caller's recorded balance in C equals the amount they sent (i.e., userBalance[caller] increases by exactly msg.value); the mutated modifier that clears the lock before the call allows reentrant attacker behavior that results in a different stored balance for the caller for some inputs.

For any caller and any sent amount, after calling addToBalance the contract's recorded userBalance for that caller equals the previous stored balance plus msg.value (i.e., addToBalance is non-reentrant and always increases caller balance by exactly msg.value); the mutant that unlocks before the call allows a reentrant attacker to call back during addToBalance and cause the final stored balance to differ.

Invariant: for every caller and any amount, after calling addToBalance from an EOA the stored userBalance equals the previous balance plus msg.value (no reentrant interference); the mutant unlocking before the body allows a reentrant attacker contract to reenter during addToBalance and make the final stored balance differ for some inputs.

For every caller and any sent amount, if the caller is a reentrant attacker that on receiving Ether calls back into addToBalance, then the reference contract's nonReentrant_ modifier prevents reentrancy so the final stored userBalance equals initial + amount, whereas the mutated modifier that unlocks before the call allows the reentrant attacker to change the final stored userBalance for some fuzzed attacker address/amount pair.

For every caller and any sent amount, after a successful addToBalance call the caller's recorded userBalance equals the prior stored balance plus msg.value (non-reentrancy ensures addToBalance is atomic); the mutant unlocking before the function body allows a reentrant attacker to break that equality for some attacker address and amount.

For any caller and any deposit amount, after withdrawBalance() returns successfully the caller's stored userBalance is zero (reference preserves zeroing even if external send fails by reverting the call); the mutant that zeroes before the external call can cause the contract to retain a non-zero stored balance when the external call reverts or fails, violating this rule.

For any caller and deposit amount, if withdrawBalance() completes successfully on the reference contract then the caller's stored userBalance becomes 0; the mutant that zeroes the balance before the external call can make withdrawBalance() revert after the call attempt while leaving the stored balance non-zero (observable via getBalance), thus violating this invariant for some adversarial callee behaviour.

For any caller and deposit amount, if the caller's external recipient reverts when receiving funds, the correct contract still keeps the caller's stored balance unchanged (so getBalance returns the pre-withdraw amount) while the mutant that zeroes before sending will cause getBalance to be 0 after the call attempt — thus the general rule: when an external transfer reverts, C preserves the stored balance; the mutant does not.

For any caller and deposit amount, if the recipient call invoked by withdrawBalance reverts, the reference C preserves the caller's stored userBalance (getBalance remains the deposited amount), whereas the mutant that zeroes the balance before the external call will set getBalance to 0 in that failing case.

For any depositor and deposit amount, if the external recipient ACCEPTS the low-level call (i.e. does not revert) then after withdrawBalance() returns successfully the depositor's recorded balance is 0; the mutant that zeroes the balance before performing the external call can cause the contract to SEND zero value (because it zeroed the balance) while still leaving the depositor's recorded balance non-zero in the reference — to distinguish them we use an adversarial recipient that ACCEPTS but does NOT actually receive funds (it drains via a reentrant-like pattern of calling withdraw on behalf of the depositor) so the reference ends with 0 recorded balance while the mutant leaves a non-zero recorded balance — the test fuzzer supplies depositor and amount to find such a case.

For any caller and any deposit amount, after calling withdrawBalance the reference contract always resets the caller's stored balance to 0, whereas the mutant that removed the state reset leaves the caller's stored balance unchanged (non-zero for positive deposits).

For any depositor and deposit amount, after a successful withdrawBalance call the reference resets that depositor's stored balance to 0; the mutant that omits the reset can leave a non‑zero balance, so there exists an input (depositor + positive deposit) where the mutant's getter returns != 0 while the reference always returns 0.

After any successful withdrawBalance call by an address that previously deposited funds, the reference contract resets that user's balance to 0 (so a subsequent view shows 0); the mutant that fails to unlock the reentrancy guard can leave the contract permanently locked but more importantly can cause withdrawBalance to revert on subsequent calls preventing the balance reset observable via the public getter for some inputs (reentrant attacker), so the rule: 'after withdrawBalance returns, getBalance(user) == 0' holds for reference but is broken by the mutant when a reentrant attacker causes differing observable behavior.

Invariant: after a caller deposits X and then calls withdrawBalance, the caller's stored userBalance remains 0 in the correct contract for every input because clearing happens after funds are sent (so visible stored balance after completion is 0); the buggy mutant that zeroes balance before sending can make userBalance for some address differ (nonzero) after withdraw due to the external call observing and re-entering or manipulating state — deploy a reentrant attacker to trigger the difference.

For any depositor and any attacker, if a depositor deposits funds then calls withdrawBalance through a reentrant attacker contract, the reference implementation always ends with c.getBalance(depositor) == 0 (balance cleared after successful withdraw), whereas the mutant that zeroes the balance before the external call can allow a reentrant attacker to manipulate the call so that some address's recorded balance is nonzero after withdraw.

For every caller and any adversarial reentrant counterparty, after caller deposits and then calls withdrawBalance, the reference contract always leaves the caller's recorded balance at 0, whereas the mutant that clears the balance before the external call can be exploited by a reentrant attacker to make the caller's recorded balance nonzero after withdraw.

For any depositor and any attacker contract address, if the depositor funds the contract and then calls withdrawBalance, the reference implementation always ends with c.getBalance(depositor) == 0 (balance cleared after the external call); the mutant that clears the balance before the external call can be exploited by a reentrant attacker to make the depositor's recorded balance nonzero after withdraw.

For any depositor address and any deposit amount, if the depositor first funds the contract and then calls withdrawBalance (possibly routed through an adversarial callee that re-enters), the reference C always ends with c.getBalance(depositor) == 0 after withdraw completes; the mutant that zeroes the balance before performing the external call can be exploited by a reentrant attacker to make c.getBalance(depositor) != 0 for some inputs.
